---
title: "Interactive analytical experiments"
subtitle: "Predict a result, change one condition, explain the evidence"
---

Each course topic has a short browser experiment. Use one when it helps a
teaching session: predict an outcome, change a relevant condition, and explain
what the new result supports. Topic units are not an assumed day-by-day timetable.

The demos run locally in the browser, with no R server or external chart service.
They are **idealised teaching models**, with their assumptions displayed. Their
controls illustrate relationships and failure cases; they do not validate a
real laboratory method.

## Choose an experiment

| Topic | Question to explore | Demo | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| From sample to answer | Does changing the amount of solution change concentration, total analyte amount, or both? | [Open](sample-answer.html) | [Read](../lessons/sample-answer.qmd) |
| Sampling and preparation | Can extra measurements repair a sampling design that misses part of the material? | [Open](sampling-preparation.html) | [Read](../lessons/sampling-preparation.qmd) |
| Error and uncertainty | Which uncertainty decreases with averaging, and which effects remain shared? | [Open](error-uncertainty.html) | [Read](../lessons/error-uncertainty.qmd) |
| Calibration and quality control | Can a plausible concentration survive a curved calibration, range failure, or failed check? | [Open](calibration-qc.html) | [Read](../lessons/calibration-qc.qmd) |
| Equilibrium and titration | How does the chosen endpoint differ from stoichiometric equivalence? | [Open](titration.html) | [Read](../lessons/titration.qmd) |
| Electrodes and potentiometry | Can a reference check pass while sample-specific activity still biases the concentration? | [Open](potentiometry.html) | [Read](../lessons/potentiometry.qmd) |
| UV and visible absorption | What happens to transmitted light and a concentration estimate when absorption or stray light changes? | [Open](uv-visible.html) | [Read](../lessons/uv-visible.qmd) |
| Matrix effects and recovery | Which matrix effects can standard addition address, and which can bias its intercept? | [Open](matrix-recovery.html) | [Read](../lessons/matrix-recovery.qmd) |
| Atomic measurements | How do background, a neighbouring line and preparation factors affect an elemental result? | [Open](atomic-methods.html) | [Read](../lessons/atomic-methods.qmd) |
| Separation principles | Can the same component amounts give peaks that no longer support separate quantification? | [Open](separations.html) | [Read](../lessons/separations.qmd) |
| GC and HPLC | When does an internal-standard ratio cancel a shared error, and when does it fail? | [Open](gc-hplc.html) | [Read](../lessons/gc-hplc.qmd) |
| Choosing and defending a result | Which evidence allows a result, and when do you need a genuinely new measurement? | [Open](defending-results.html) | [Read](../lessons/defending-results.qmd) |

## Use the experiment to build an explanation

1. State a prediction before moving a control. Give the direction and chemical
   reason, not only a numerical guess.
2. Change one condition. Inspect the plot and the result or reporting decision.
3. Try a failure case. Explain what additional evidence or measurement would
   be needed before reporting the quantity.
4. Reset, export a CSV, and reproduce one relationship in R. Keep the units,
   model assumptions, sample/preparation roles and withheld-result reasons.

Some controls affect the underlying sample or measurement conditions; others
represent an analyst's assumption or decision. Do not treat changing a planned
preparation as a replacement for a new measured signal.

## Take simulated data back to R

The **Export CSV** button saves the current scenario's data. Move the file into
your course project and import it using the familiar workflow:

```{r}
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
# Replace with the filename you exported and saved in your project:
# demo <- read_csv("data/my-demo.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
# glimpse(demo)
```

Read the exported column names and the model notes before fitting a line or
calculating uncertainty. Some CSVs contain both a diagnostic candidate estimate
and the supported result; a withheld estimate must not become zero. Model
curves and time/wavelength positions are not independent sampled materials.

Controls use ordinary labelled form elements and work with the keyboard.
Charts can be inspected by pointing, or by focusing a chart and using its left
and right arrow keys. The model notes and live text interpretation accompany
the graphics.
